methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict series wins?
How should adherence be defined, and is it separable from roster talent and coaching quality?
Is the recommended mix derived from the same play-by-play used to score adherence and outcomes (outcome-derived labels, leakage)?
Is a series-level test with 54 units adequately powered, and how should multiplicity be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Recorded hypothesis: teams that run BEST counters more (and AVOID less) after suppression win more series. Result: BEST run rate vs won Spearman rho=+0.131 (p=0.1723); AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 (p=0.3099); mean PPP BEST 1.395 vs AVOID 0.865. Failure type A_unanswerable; INSUFF_EVIDENCE is 91.5% of triggers; n=110 series-directions.

Recorded hypothesis: pct_ran_BEST minus pct_ran_AVOID predicts series wins after controlling for regular-season net-rating talent. Talent is a significant per-series predictor (logistic p=0.0213; team-in-series cluster p=0.0095); adaptation is not (p=0.2755 after talent control; univariate beta=+0.311, p=0.1128). corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. Failure type A_unanswerable, attributed to confounding with roster quality at n=55 series.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap on initiator-filtered H2 possessions: mean gap +0.427 PPP (BEST 1.347, 38 players; AVOID 0.920, 94 players) at n>=10 per tier. Only 3 players clear n>=30 in both tiers. Recorded as positive, but the record is about per-player possession gaps, not series outcomes.

Playoff adaptation-pair sustainability: 10/12 pairs CONSISTENT and within 0.10 PPP of non-pivot; two pairs with enough signal were PIVOT_LOSES (PNR->PULL_UP 1.069 vs 1.224, n_matchups=9; DRIVE->PULL_UP 1.101 vs 1.217, n=5). Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null), with pair n_matchups 5 to 44.
Season stability of top sequential suppressors: only 2/30 stars (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule. Recorded as B_powered_null, min n=20 per cell.

Three-level counter ranking (population vs team vs matchup): the best counter after a suppressed play type was not stable across levels in the recorded L1 vs L2 comparison (e.g., DRIVE: L1 best CUT, L2 MIA best PNR). Cells had small n (L1 n_mu 5 to 696; playoff n_matchups 4 to 44). No validation recorded.

Superstar suppression profiles: rank-1 suppressor 'varies meaningfully across players'; most rank-1 deltas were within 1 to 2 SE; no multiple-comparison control; an OTHER artifact was flagged in the document.

Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK is the top suppressor for 6+ stars in the recorded cells (e.g., D. Mitchell d=-0.294, n_after=95), but several cells have n_after of 32 to 95; no multiplicity correction; mechanism unclear; no validation recorded.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gaps (exploratory) across 78 players with at least 5 rows per tier; gaps range from strongly positive to negative with small n per player; no multiplicity or clustered test; flagged for placebo dependence.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type: large lineup and play-type PPP gaps for named stars (e.g., Jokic vs MIN 0.814, -0.385, n=59); no placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether BEST/AVOID run-rate alignment predicts series wins (direct adherence-to-winning test at series level)
failed_approaches.why: Alignment-win Spearmans were not significant (p=0.172 and p=0.310) at n=110 series-directions; the question was classed A_unanswerable, and most triggers were INSUFF_EVIDENCE (91.5%).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing series wins to coaching adaptation after controlling for talent
failed_approaches.why: After talent control the adaptation term was not significant (p=0.275); with n of about 55 series, coaching adaptation could not be separated from roster quality (confounding, A_unanswerable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pivoting to a listed counter after suppression sustaining higher PPP
failed_approaches.why: Pivoting was not better than staying in 10/12 pairs and was worse in two pairs with enough signal; recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Season stability of top suppressors as a basis for a stable recommended mix
failed_approaches.why: Only 2/30 stars met the stability rule; recorded as B_powered_null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using a league-default best counter, stable across population, team, and matchup levels
failed_approaches.why: The best counter was not stable across levels in the recorded comparison; cells were small (inconclusive, small sample and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks).
Deltas were mostly within 1 to 2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control (inconclusive).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naming lineup and forced-play-type suppressors for stars
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts (not a hypothesis test).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests the exact question (adherence to a suppression-conditional mix predicting series wins) with a fitted adherence measure and a pre-specified series-level test.

The closest series-level tests (FAM:SF-APPS-030, FAM:SF-APPS-027) found no significant association between BEST/AVOID alignment or adaptation and series wins, and both were classed untestable on power or confounding grounds.
Talent (regular-season net rating) was the stronger series-level predictor in FAM:SF-APPS-027, so any adherence effect is confounded with roster quality unless talent is controlled.

Play-type suppression and counter-ranking findings in this program repeatedly failed to survive power, stability, or multiplicity checks (FAM:SF-APPA-058, FAM:SF-APPM-054, FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPM-055).
Only player-level, possession-level gaps were recorded as supported (FAM:SF-APPS-036), and that record does not address series outcomes.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence predicts winning in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data, because no record fits adherence against series outcomes with a pre-registered design.
The direction or size of any adherence effect after controlling for talent, coaching, and opponent quality.
Whether a team-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap exists as a series-level predictor; FAM:SF-APPS-036 mentions a team-level gap but no team-level record was retrieved.
Whether the recommended mix is out-of-sample or was derived from the same outcome data, which determines whether adherence scores are leaky.
Anything about the 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial on the question date (complete only from 2026-06-21).
own_inferences: With 54 series units and a binary win outcome, the power to detect a modest adherence effect is very low; even a moderate effect would be hard to distinguish from zero.
If the recommended mix is estimated from the same play-by-play and seasons that define adherence and outcomes, adherence will be partly determined by the outcome (leakage and outcome-derived label).
Adherence is likely correlated with team quality and playing time, so raw adherence-win correlations would mostly reflect talent (confounding).
Series are clustered by team, so team-season effects may dominate; a per-series test would overstate independence.
The 2025-26 playoff sample is incomplete on the question date, so including it would introduce a truncation artifact.
uncertainties: The task states 54 series units, but FAM:SF-APPS-030 and FAM:SF-APPS-027 record n=55 series (110 directions); the reason for the difference is not recorded.
The details of how the suppression-conditional recommended mix was built (in-sample or out-of-sample) are not in the task statement or the retrieved records.
Fields in the per-game files cover play-by-play and lineups, but whether adherence can be measured per series from them is not confirmed.
Several retrieved records were cut off mid-text, so some details (e.g., the full SF-APPS-036 team-level comparison) were not read; read_family was not called.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval showed that the closest prior series-level tests were untestable or null, that talent confounding was already a documented failure, and that the program's suppression and counter findings repeatedly failed on power, stability, or multiplicity. This moved the decision from a proceed-as-posed test to do_not_proceed, with a minimum viable test specified.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series units give very low power to detect a modest adherence-to-win effect; the closest prior series test (FAM:SF-APPS-030, n=110 directions) was already non-significant and untestable.
Adherence is confounded with roster talent and coaching; FAM:SF-APPS-027 showed talent dominates adaptation as a series predictor.
The recommended mix is derived from the same play-by-play used to score adherence and outcomes, so the label is partly outcome-derived.
If the mix is estimated using games that occur before or during the series being scored, adherence uses future information.
Four seasons with changing play-type usage and rules make a pooled mix non-stationary; the 2025-26 playoffs are incomplete on the question date.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work by this project addressed closely related questions: alignment of BEST/AVOID run rates with series wins (null, untestable), coaching adaptation controlling for talent (not significant after talent control, untestable), and pivoting sustainability (adequately powered null). None tests the exact adherence-to-winning question with a pre-specified design, so the question is partly but not fully answered by prior work.

risks.text: 54 series (about 110 team-directions) is too few for a reliable test of a modest effect; the closest prior test was underpowered.
Talent, coaching, and opponent quality confound adherence and wins (FAM:SF-APPS-027).
The recommended mix comes from the same play-by-play as the outcome, so adherence is partly defined by results.
Mixes estimated with data from the scored series or later would leak outcome information.
Teams that adhere to a recommendation may be selected on prior form or on the match-up, producing regression-to-the-mean effects in apparent adherence benefits.
Many play types, levels (population, team, matchup), and sequential triggers were examined in this program with no multiplicity control (FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Named-star and player-level gaps were not checked against placebo or matched controls (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-048).
Play-type PPP cells have small n (5 to 50 per cell), so adherence and suppression measures may be unreliable.
Play-type usage changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-06-16.
The series count differs between the task (54) and the records (55); the series-to-unit mapping must be verified before analysis.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-specified, out-of-sample adherence score (share of a team's counters matching its suppression-conditional recommended mix) and series win, conditional on regular-season net rating, reported with an interval; not a causal effect.
design.unit: Team-series (each series contributes two directions, analysed with clustering by team and season).
design.sample: Only completed series from 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs plus completed 2025-26 series after the playoff data are complete (not before 2026-06-21). Target is 54 series, reconciled with the 55 recorded in prior records.
design.power: Before any analysis, compute the minimum detectable effect for 54 series; if it exceeds a plausible effect size, report the study as descriptive. Do not claim a null from an underpowered test.
design.controls: Regular-season net rating, home advantage, coaching tenure, opponent strength, and rotation minutes; adherence built from the mix estimated on seasons strictly before the scored series (no in-sample mix).
design.falsification: Placebo adherence from randomly permuted mixes and from the mix of a non-playing opponent; the adherence effect must exceed the placebo distribution.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (adherence coefficient, pre-registered); all other play types and levels are exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Primary: support only if the adherence coefficient's 95% clustered interval excludes zero and exceeds the placebo range; otherwise report as null or inconclusive with the minimum detectable effect.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs (complete); 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded unless complete (from 2026-06-21). Per-game files from the NBA stats API; play-type possession records from the graph database.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict winning?
How should adherence be measured and validated against outcomes at the series level with 54 units?
What confounding and outcome-derived label risks arise when the recommended mix is derived from the same play-by-play data?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
